source.title: Discrepancy estimates for sequences: new results and open problems

accepted.question_text: For the d-dimensional lattice point set (({n a1/N}, ..., {n ad/N})) for n=0,1,...,N-1, prove an average-type lower bound showing that for every chi < 1 there is a constant C'_chi > 0 such that, for all N, the discrepancy D_N is at least C'_chi (log N)^(d-1) log log N / N for at least chi N^d choices of the integer vector (a1,...,ad) with 0 <= a1,...,ad < N.
accepted.context_brief: Average lower bounds for lattice point sets

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1 Show that for every χ < 1 there is a constant C′χ > 0 such that for all N for the discrepancy DN of the lattice point set ... we have DN ≥ C′χ (log N)^(d−1) log log N / N for at least χN^d choices for (a1, . . . , ad) with 0 ≤ a1, . . . , ad < N.

accepted.question_text: Fix integers d >= 1 and m >= 2 and a prime base q. Show that there exists a constant B~(d,q) > 0 such that, for every delta with 0 < delta < 1, at least a proportion 1-delta of all d-tuples C=(C1,...,Cd) of m x m matrices over Z_q that generate digital nets have discrepancy D_N satisfying D_N >= delta B~(d,q) (log N)^(d-1) log log N / N for infinitely many N.
accepted.context_brief: Average lower bounds for digital nets

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2 Show that for given integers d ≥ 1, m ≥ 2 and prime base q there exists a constant B˜(d, q) > 0 such that: for all δ with 0 < δ < 1, the number of d-tuples C = (C1, . . . , Cd) of m×m-matrices, providing a digital net over Zq with discrepancy DN satisfying DN ≥ δB˜(d, q) (log N)^(d−1) log log N / N for infinitely many N, is at least (1 − δ)#Md(m).

accepted.question_text: For digital nets generated by rational functions over finite fields, prove an average-type lower bound for the discrepancy analogous to the lower-bound statement asked for in Open Problem 2 for ordinary digital nets over Z_q.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3 Give an average-type lower bound (in the style as stated in the Open Problem 2) for the discrepancy of digital nets generated by rational functions over finite fields.

accepted.question_text: Find, for a suitable function phi, an asymptotic formula with a small error term R_chi for the counting function N(h; a1,...,ad), which counts integer vectors (n1,...,nd) with -h <= n1,...,nd <= h and fractional part {n1 a1/N + ... + nd ad/N} < phi(n1,...,nd), such that for every chi < 1 and every h in N one has N(h; a1,...,ad) = sum_{-h <= n1,...,nd < h} phi(n1,...,nd) + R_chi(h) for at least chi N^d choices of (a1,...,ad) with 0 <= a1,...,ad < N.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4 Find (for suitable φ) an asymptotic representation with a “small” error-term Rχ for N(h; a1, . . . , ad) := # { -h ≤ n1, . . . , nd ≤ h | { n1 a1/N + n2 a2/N + . . . + nd ad/N } < φ(n1, . . . , nd) } ... For all χ < 1 and all h ∈ N we have N(h; a1, . . . , ad) = Σ φ(n1, . . . , nd) + Rχ(h) for at least χN^d choices of (a1, . . . , ad).

accepted.question_text: Given positive integers d1,...,dl with d1+...+dl=d and pairwise coprime bases q1,...,ql, determine functions g(N) as small as possible and f(N) as large as possible such that, for almost all d-dimensional Halton-Niederreiter sequences whose i-th component is a d_i-dimensional digital sequence in base q_i, the discrepancy D_N satisfies D_N = Omega(f(N)) and D_N = O(g(N)).

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5 For given d1, . . . , dl ∈ N with d1+. . .+dl = d and given coprime bases q1, . . . , ql determine g(N) as small as possible and f(N) as large as possible such that we have: for the discrepancy DN of almost all Halton-Niederreiter sequences with di-dimensional components in base qi; i = 1, . . . , l we have DN = Ω(f(N)) and DN = O(g(N)).

accepted.question_text: Under the same decomposition d=d1+...+dl and coprime bases q1,...,ql, determine the sharp metrical discrepancy orders for finite-row Halton-Niederreiter sequences: find g(N) as small as possible and f(N) as large as possible so that, with respect to a suitable measure on finite-row generating matrices, almost all such sequences satisfy D_N = Omega(f(N)) and D_N = O(g(N)).

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6 For given d1, . . . , dl with d1 + . . . + dl = d and given coprime bases q1, . . . , ql determine g(N) as small as possible and f(N) as large as possible such that we have: for the discrepancy DN of almost all finite-row Halton-Niederreiter sequences (with respect to a suitable measure) ... we have DN = Ω(f(N)) and DN = O(g(N)).

accepted.question_text: Study the discrepancy of explicit Halton-Kronecker sequences, for example the two-dimensional sequence z_n = (x_n, {n sqrt(2)}) where x_n is the one-dimensional Halton sequence in base 2, that is, the van der Corput sequence. The goal is to understand the discrepancy behavior of concrete, not merely metric-almost-all, Halton-Kronecker examples.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7 Study the discrepancy of concrete Halton-Kronecker sequences, as for example (xn, {n√2})n≥0 with (xn)n≥0 the van der Corput sequence.

accepted.question_text: Let A_K be the largest partial quotient in the continued-fraction expansion of 2^K sqrt(2) for K=1,2,..., and let B_L = max_{K<=L} A_K. Obtain sharp bounds for the growth of B_L.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8 Let AK denote the largest continued fraction coefficient of 2^K√2 for K = 1, 2, . . .. Give sharp bounds for the growth behaviour of BL := max K≤L AK.

accepted.question_text: Improve Kritzer's discrepancy bound for hybrid point sets obtained by combining a Hammersley point set with a good lattice point set, gaining almost a logarithmic factor over the bound stated in Theorem 3.2.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9 Improve the result of Kritzer cited in Theorem 3.2 above on the discrepancy of Hammersley-good lattice point-sets by almost a logarithmic factor.

accepted.question_text: For the concrete sequence z_n = (x_n, {n sqrt(2)}) where x_n is the van der Corput sequence in base 2, prove a lower bound D_N >= c (log N)^2 / N for some constant c > 0 for infinitely many N.
accepted.context_brief: Lower bound for a concrete hybrid sequence

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10 Show for the sequence of Problem 7, namely (xn, {n√2})n≥0, where (xn)n≥1 is the van der Corput-sequence in base 2, that DN ≥ c (log N)^2 / N holds for a constant c > 0 and infinitely many N.

accepted.question_text: Let x_n be the van der Corput sequence in base 2. Show that for almost all real alpha there exists a constant C(alpha) > 0 such that the discrepancy of the hybrid sequence z_n = (x_n, {n alpha}) satisfies D_N >= C(alpha) (log N)^2 / N for infinitely many N.
accepted.context_brief: Metrical lower bound for hybrid sequences

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11 Show for the discrepancy DN of the sequences (xn, {nα}n≥0) where (xn)n≥0 is the van der Corput sequence in base 2, that for almost all α there is a C(α) > 0 such that DN ≥ C(α) (log N)^2 / N holds for infinitely many N.

accepted.question_text: Obtain an essentially sharp upper metrical bound for the discrepancy of Niederreiter-Kronecker hybrid sequences z_n = (x_n, {n alpha}) where x_n is a fixed s-dimensional digital sequence generated by finite-row matrices and ({n alpha}) is a t-dimensional Kronecker sequence, with the bound required to hold for almost all alpha.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 12 Give an essentially sharp upper metrical bound for the discrepancy of Niederreiter-Kronecker sequences zn = (xn, {nα})n≥0 where (xn)n≥0 is a given digital s-dimensional sequence generated by matrices with finite rows, and ({nα})n≥0 is a t-dimensional Kronecker sequence, which is valid for almost all α.

accepted.question_text: Let ({n alpha}) be a one-dimensional Kronecker sequence and let x_n be the one-dimensional base-2 digital sequence generated by the infinite matrix whose first row is all 1s and whose later rows form the identity shift shown in the paper. Determine sharp metrical upper bounds, and if possible also sharp metrical lower bounds, for the discrepancy of the hybrid sequence z_n = (x_n, {n alpha}) for almost all real alpha.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13 Give sharp metrical upper - and, if possible, also lower - bounds for the discrepancy of the sequence zn = (xn, {nα})n≥0 where ({nα})n≥0 is a one-dimensional Kronecker sequence, and where (xn)n≥0 is the one-dimensional digital sequence in base 2 generated by the matrix ... The estimates should hold for almost all α ∈ R.

accepted.question_text: Let n_k be the increasing sequence of positive integers for which the sum S_2(n_k) of the binary digits of n_k is even. Determine the exact metrical order of discrepancy of the one-dimensional sequence ({n_k alpha})_{k>=0}.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 14 Give the exact metrical order of the discrepancy of the sequence ({nkα})k≥0, where (nk)k≥0 denotes the increasing sequence of positive integers nk for which S2(nk) ≡ 0 mod 2 holds, where S2(n) denotes the sum of digits of n in base 2.

accepted.question_text: Work out in detail the program sketched in the paper for using hybrid sequences in the J.P. Morgan Credit Metrics credit-risk simulation system: choose a dimension s<d for which an s-dimensional low-discrepancy sequence with N points is preferable to pseudorandom simulation, identify the s credits contributing most to portfolio risk, run the Credit Metrics simulation using quasi-Monte Carlo coordinates for those high-risk credits and pseudorandom coordinates for the remaining credits, and analyze the resulting performance against pure Monte Carlo and pure quasi-Monte Carlo methods.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15 Carry out the above sketched program for using hybrid sequences in the credit risk management program Credit Metrics in detail and analyse the performance in comparison with pure Monte Carlo or pure quasi-Monte Carlo methods.

accepted.question_text: Let c be the largest constant such that every sequence (x_n) in [0,1) satisfies D_N^* >= c log N / N for infinitely many N. Improve the currently known bounds 0.06015... <= c <= 0.222... and determine c more sharply.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 16 Let c be maximal such that for every sequence (xn)n≥0 in [0, 1) we have D∗N ≥ c log N / N for infinitely many N. Improve the best until now known bounds 0.06015 . . . ≤ c ≤ 0.222 . . . for c.

accepted.question_text: Show that every two-dimensional digital sequence in base 2 has discrepancy at least c (log N)^2 / N for infinitely many N for some constant c>0, or at least establish this lower bound for a substantial subclass such as NUT sequences or finite-row sequences.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 17 Show that for all 2-dimensional digital sequences in base 2 we have DN ≥ c (log N)^2 / N for infinitely many N. Or, show this estimate at least for a certain class of such (low-discrepancy) sequences (e.g. for NUT sequences or finite-row sequences).

accepted.question_text: Obtain an improved lower bound for the discrepancy of the two-dimensional Halton sequence, and ideally decide whether its true discrepancy order is (log N)^2 / N or not.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 18 Give an improved lower bound for the discrepancy of the Halton sequence in dimension 2. In the best case decide whether the right order of the discrepancy is (log N)^2 / N, or not.

accepted.question_text: Determine the correct order of the best general lower bound for discrepancy that holds for all sequences in the d-dimensional unit cube [0,1)^d.

evidence.quote: determine the correct order of the best general lower bound for discrepancy, holding for all sequences in [0, 1)d

accepted.question_text: Is the sequence ({(3/2)^n}) for n>=0 uniformly distributed in the interval [0,1), or not?

evidence.quote: is the sequence {(3/2)^n}n≥0 uniformly distributed in [0, 1) or not?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist real numbers alpha and beta such that the two-dimensional Kronecker sequence ({n alpha}, {n beta}) has low discrepancy, meaning that D_N <= C (log N)^2 / N for all N for some constant C?

evidence.quote: do there exist α, β ∈ R such that the 2-dimensional Kronecker sequence ({nα}, {nβ})n≥0 is a low-discrepancy sequence, i.e., satisfies DN ≤ C (log N)^2 / N for all N, or not?

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record to arXiv:1407.2380 and mapped the PDF. The open-problem region is concentrated on pages 7-15, including Open Problems 1-18 and three additional explicit questions in Section 4.
Extracted 21 candidates: 18 numbered open problems and 3 additional explicit open questions from the miscellaneous section.

Rewrote each candidate into a standalone question while keeping the mathematical setting and asymptotic targets explicit and preserving the source's terminology where it is already self-contained in the quoted statement.
Kept the 21 extracted questions as distinct items; no near-duplicate merge was needed because each problem asks for a different discrepancy bound, model, or sequence class.
Accepted all 21 items because each has an explicit problem statement in the paper together with page-locatable quote evidence and no unresolved cross-reference needed for the rewritten question text.
